```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
librarian::shelf(DT, dplyr, ggplot2, glue, here, knitr, readr, tidyr, quiet = T)
source(here("libs/bench_ai_readiness/score.R"))

dir_out   <- here("data/bench_ai_readiness")
runs_root <- Sys.getenv("BENCH_RUNS_DIR", "~/_big/bench_ai_runs")
run_tag   <- sub("_$", "", params$run_prefix)
csv_runs  <- file.path(dir_out, glue("runs_{run_tag}.csv"))
csv_ref   <- file.path(dir_out, "reference_answers.csv")
COND      <- c("closed", "raw", "release")
```

```{r}
#| label: load
q   <- read_bench_questions()
ref <- if (file.exists(csv_ref)) read_csv(csv_ref, col_types = cols(reference = "c")) else {
  r <- bench_reference(q) |> select(id, tier, kind, tol_abs, tol_rel, reference)
  write_csv(r, csv_ref, na = ""); r }

# sessions: summarized from the transcripts when they are on this machine, else the tracked csv
runs <- if (dir.exists(path.expand(runs_root))) {
  r <- collect_bench_configs(runs_root, glue("^{params$run_prefix}")); write_csv(r, csv_runs, na = ""); r
} else read_csv(csv_runs, col_types = cols(answer = "c"))

scored <- score_bench_runs(runs, ref) |>
  mutate(config    = glue("{model} / {effort}"),
         condition = factor(condition, COND))

# accuracy per configuration x condition: mean over sessions, and the spread over the repeats
acc_rep <- scored |> group_by(config, model, effort, condition, rep) |>
  summarize(pct = 100 * mean(correct), cost = sum(cost_usd, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
acc <- scored |> group_by(config, model, effort, condition) |>
  summarize(n = n(), pct = 100 * mean(correct),
            cost_usd = mean(cost_usd, na.rm = TRUE), minutes = mean(seconds, na.rm = TRUE) / 60, .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(acc_rep |> group_by(config, condition) |>
              summarize(rep_min = min(pct), rep_max = max(pct), rep_sd = sd(pct), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("config", "condition"))
n_q    <- nrow(q)
n_reps <- max(scored$rep)
n_cfg  <- n_distinct(scored$config)
rng    <- \(cnd, col = "pct") { x <- acc[[col]][acc$condition == cnd]; c(min(x), max(x)) }
```

## Summary

Duncan Watson-Parris asked for a pilot of the benchmark proposed in Aim 2: about 20–30 questions about
the data, put to off-the-shelf models, with performance summarized in a sentence or two as preliminary
data. This notebook runs that pilot and keeps every step reproducible.

We put `r n_q` questions to `r n_cfg` model × effort configurations, `r n_reps` times each, under three
conditions:

- **closed-book**: no tools and no data, so the model answers from training alone.
- **raw**: the providers' public sources, as a user finds them today (ERDDAP, CalCOFI.org, EDI, NCEI).
  This is the pilot's stand-in for the proposal's "release 0".
- **release**: integrated release v2026.10.21 as a local DuckDB database, with no network.

Accuracy across configurations:

- closed-book: `r paste(round(rng("closed")), collapse = "–")`%
- raw: `r paste(round(rng("raw")), collapse = "–")`%
- release: `r paste(round(rng("release")), collapse = "–")`%

### Sentence for the proposal

```{r}
#| label: sentence
#| results: asis
tier_rng <- scored |> group_by(config, condition, tier) |> summarize(pct = 100 * mean(correct), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(condition, tier) |> summarize(lo = round(min(pct)), hi = round(max(pct)), .groups = "drop")
r  <- \(cnd) { x <- round(rng(cnd)); if (x[1] == x[2]) glue("{x[1]}%") else glue("{x[1]}–{x[2]}%") }
models <- paste(unique(sub("-5-5$", " 5.5", tools::toTitleCase(scored$model))), collapse = ", ")

# raw vs release per configuration: accuracy gain, and the cut in cost and median time per answer
vs <- scored |> filter(condition != "closed") |>
  group_by(config, model, condition) |>
  summarize(pct = 100 * mean(correct), usd = mean(cost_usd, na.rm = TRUE), sec = median(seconds, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(pct, usd, sec)) |>
  mutate(gain = pct_release - pct_raw, usd_cut = 100 * (1 - usd_release / usd_raw), sec_cut = 100 * (1 - sec_release / sec_raw))
pr  <- \(x) { x <- round(range(x)); if (x[1] == x[2]) glue("{x[1]}%") else glue("{x[1]}–{x[2]}%") }
big <- vs |> filter(model == "opus-5-5")
sml <- vs |> filter(model == "haiku-5-5")
sentence <- glue(
  "In a pilot of {n_q} questions about CalCOFI data (retrieval, cross-dataset integration, analysis and ",
  "unanswerable items) put to off-the-shelf models ({models}; {n_cfg} model and effort settings, {n_reps} runs each), ",
  "the models answered {r('closed')} correctly from training alone, {r('raw')} when they had to find and download ",
  "the providers' public files themselves, and {r('release')} with the integrated release, which also cut the cost ",
  "per answer by {pr(vs$usd_cut)} and the median time by {pr(vs$sec_cut)}. ",
  "The release helped the smaller models most (Haiku 5.5: {round(sml$pct_raw)}% to {round(sml$pct_release)}%); ",
  "the strongest agents ({round(min(big$pct_raw))}% from raw files) matched it and, in doing so, exposed a ",
  "cruise-key defect in the release, the kind of release-to-release check Aim 2 proposes.")
cat("> ", sentence, "\n")
writeLines(sentence, file.path(dir_out, glue("sentence_{run_tag}.txt")))
```

## Why this pilot

The proposal's Aim 2 scores the *data*, not the agent. Existing benchmarks for data-driven science
hold the data fixed and compare agents: DiscoveryBench (Majumder et al., 2024), BLADE (Gu et al., 2024)
and ScienceAgentBench (Chen et al., 2025). Aim 2 instead holds the agent fixed and asks how much each
release improves what it can do. Five AI reviewers of the draft (punch-list row 2) said a small pilot
would be the strongest preliminary result the text could add. This pilot reproduces the Aim 2 design
at small scale:

- the three tiers of questions, plus traps and unanswerable items
- reference answers written as code
- repeated runs on several pinned models and effort levels
- a closed-book condition
- a raw-source baseline

## Design

```{r}
#| label: tbl-questions
#| tbl-cap: "The pilot questions, with the reference answer computed in SQL against release v2026.10.21."
q |>
  left_join(ref |> select(id, reference), by = "id") |>
  mutate(reference = case_when(
    kind == "none"   ~ "NOT AVAILABLE",
    kind == "number" ~ as.character(signif(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(reference)), 5)),
    TRUE             ~ reference)) |>
  select(id, tier, question = text, reference) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 30, dom = "t"))
```

**Questions.** There are eight retrieval questions (one value from one dataset) and seven integration
questions that join datasets at the same cruise and station:

- bottle × ichthyoplankton
- ZooScan × bottle
- CTD × ichthyoplankton
- the cruise and ship reference
- a taxonomic join between the ichthyoplankton and mesopelagic-fish datasets

There are six analysis questions:

- anomalies relative to a 1993–2013 station-by-month baseline
- linear trends
- a mean larval density where tows with no catch must count as zero. The ichthyoplankton records list
  only positive catches, so this one is a trap.
- a correlation

Three questions cannot be answered from the data:

- nitrate before 1959
- bottle pH in 1985
- CalBOBL bongo tows in 1972, before the bongo net replaced the ring net in 1977–78

The reference SQL for each question is in `libs/bench_ai_readiness/questions.yml`.

**Reference answers** are the question's SQL run on the release. Where the raw sessions agreed with each
other and disagreed with the release, we traced the difference to its source. In one case (finding 4
under [Raw vs. release disagreements](#raw-vs.-release-disagreements)) the release was wrong, and the
reference SQL now corrects for it. Elsewhere a legitimate difference between a provider's file and the
release still scores the raw answer wrong, so the pilot stays conservative for the raw condition.

**Sessions.** Each session is one headless Claude Code run (`claude -p`, version 2.1.314). It loads no
`CLAUDE.md`, memory, skills or MCP servers, and runs inside Claude Code's OS sandbox:

- it can write only to its own folder
- it cannot read the CalCOFI repositories, the other condition's runs or, in the raw condition, the
  release copy
- network access is limited to the providers' domains in the raw condition, and is off in the release
  condition

Every tool call is checked afterwards for any reach past the session's condition (@tbl-audit). A session
had 4 min (closed), 20 min (release) or 40 min (raw), and had to end with `FINAL ANSWER: <value>` or
`FINAL ANSWER: NOT AVAILABLE`. Numbers are scored within the tolerance stated per question, and
unanswerable items only by declining. The runner is `libs/bench_ai_readiness/run_agents.sh` and the
scorer is `libs/bench_ai_readiness/score.R`.

## Results

```{r}
#| label: fig-accuracy
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy by condition for each model and effort setting. Points are the repeats (each over all questions); bars are their mean."
ggplot(acc_rep, aes(condition, pct, color = condition)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "col", fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~config) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(closed = "#8c8c8c", raw = "#d95f02", release = "#1b6ca8"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% correct") + ylim(0, 100) + theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-accuracy
#| tbl-cap: "Accuracy (% of sessions correct) by configuration, condition and tier; spread across repeats; mean cost and time per answer."
scored |>
  group_by(config, condition, tier) |> summarize(pct = round(100 * mean(correct)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = tier, values_from = pct) |>
  left_join(acc |> transmute(config, condition, all = round(pct),
                             `repeats (min–max)` = glue("{round(rep_min)}–{round(rep_max)}"),
                             `USD/answer` = round(cost_usd, 2), `min/answer` = round(minutes, 1)),
            by = c("config", "condition")) |>
  arrange(config, condition) |>
  select(config, condition, retrieval, integration, analysis, unanswerable, everything()) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-by-question
#| tbl-cap: "Sessions correct per question and condition, pooled over configurations and repeats."
scored |>
  group_by(id, condition) |>
  summarize(cell = glue("{sum(correct)}/{n()}"), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = cell) |>
  left_join(ref |> select(id, tier, reference), by = "id") |>
  mutate(id = factor(id, q$id)) |> arrange(id) |>
  select(id, tier, reference, any_of(COND)) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-answers
#| tbl-cap: "Every session's answer (searchable)."
scored |>
  select(config, condition, id, rep, answer, reference, correct, cost_usd, seconds) |>
  arrange(id, condition, config, rep) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE))
```

### Audit

```{r}
#| label: tbl-audit
#| tbl-cap: "Tool calls per configuration and condition, and calls that named a resource outside the condition (expected 0)."
scored |>
  group_by(config, condition) |>
  summarize(sessions = n(), completed = sum(completed), tool_calls = sum(n_tool_calls),
            forbidden_calls = sum(n_forbidden), sandbox_denials = sum(n_sandbox_deny), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable()
```

## Limitations

- `r n_q` questions is a pilot of the method, not a measurement of the release. The proposal's benchmark
  has about 250 questions, an open-weights model, human baselines and a held-out set.
- The models are all from one family (Claude). Closed-book scores also depend on what each model saw in
  training.
- The reference answers come from the release under test, so a release defect shared by the reference
  and the release condition goes unnoticed unless the raw sessions disagree. They caught one here
  (finding 4); others may remain. In the full benchmark, a second scientist writes the reference code
  against the authoritative sources.
- The questions were written by someone who knows the release, and most of them can be answered from
  the providers' well-documented ERDDAP services. This favours neither condition by design, but it is
  not a sample of the questions users ask.
- The release condition gets a plain DuckDB file with a three-line README. It has none of the AI layer
  the proposal would build: no MCP tools, no semantic metadata, no method register.

## Reproduce

```bash
# 1. local copy of the release (about 600 MB of parquet, plus views)
libs/bench_ai_readiness/build_release_db.sh v2026.10.21 ~/_big/bench_ai_release
# 2. sessions per configuration: questions x conditions x 3 repeats
for cfg in "sonnet-5-5 default" "sonnet-5-5 low" "opus-5-5 medium" "opus-5-5 high" "haiku-5-5 default"; do
  set -- $cfg
  libs/bench_ai_readiness/run_agents.sh "2026-10-30_$1_$2" "release raw closed" 3 6 "claude-$1" "$2"
done
# 3. this notebook: reference answers, scoring, tables
quarto render bench_ai_readiness.qmd
```

The transcripts of every session are archived as `bench_ai_runs_2026-10-30.tar.gz` beside the proposal
drafts. The tracked summary is `data/bench_ai_readiness/runs_2026-10-30.csv`.
